assumptions: The retention tag is retained, the template's example, since no tag exists in the workspace
A scheduled task with db.del/db.bulk.delete counts as cleanup for the rule
The 2-year period is stated in the statement, not enforced by a param (no param takes a duration)
Tags gdpr and storage-limitation on the policy record the framework criterion; they do not claim compliance
confusions: Template tag example 'retained' is on no table in this workspace; the skill says a rule must not add a tag, so the policy selects nothing until the owner tags tables. Not clear whether the parser's warning is enough to flag this to the customer or whether a policy should be held until the tag exists.

The check's table_selector parameter (tables in scope) and the template's tags param are different things; the template fill tags is passed to the check's top-level tags scope, and I was not certain that is the intended mapping for table.coverage_required.

The skill says a deletion rule could be a candidate for object.test_coverage or a function-level check, but no check verifies that a deletion statement reaches every table holding a user's data; I could not find one.
wished_for: A check that verifies a deletion function (or the account DELETE endpoint) reaches every table tagged personal data, or a way to scope table.coverage_required to a named function
A retention-period param or a check that reads the age filter in a cleanup task's where clause
Guidance on whether a policy should be written when its tag does not exist yet on any table (inert vs. held)
A recipe for GDPR storage limitation and right to erasure combining RET-002 with tagging conventions
parse_errors_seen: RET-002.R1: tags "retained" is on no table on this branch, so it selects nothing (warning, exit 0)
why_confidence: The policy covers only the cleanup-task part of the retention ask. It does not enforce 2 years, it selects nothing until tables are tagged, and nothing checks that account deletion reaches all personal data. I did not run evaluate, so no outcome is verified.
